evidence: The new AC premise in Example/Given and direct def-axiom-of-choice dependency repair the previously invalid [L1] invocation. But Verification 1.1 asserts without derivation that an arbitrary central extension is determined by a parameter a=tilde(x)^n, and 2.1 only shows how a changes when the lift changes; it does not construct an extension for every a or prove that this is the entire equivalence relation. For n>=1, construct E_a=(A direct-sum Z)/<(-a,n)>, prove A injects and E_a/A=C_n, and show every extension is isomorphic via (b,m)->b tilde(x)^m; changing lifts yields a+nb. Then [L1] identifies the resulting A/nA classes with H^2. No file/stamp edit made by this reviewer.

The new AC premise in Example/Given and direct dependency exactly match [L1]. Each group has center C2 and quotient C2 x C2; D8 has five involutions and Q8 has one, so no middle-group isomorphism and hence no extension equivalence exists. The AC-qualified classification sends them to distinct H^2 classes. No file/stamp edit made by this reviewer.

Independent reread of the final proof: n>=1 makes A->E_a injective in E_a=(A x Z)/<(-a,n)>; quotient by A is C_n and the distinguished generator has nth power a. For arbitrary central E, (b,m)->b tilde(x)^m is surjective and has kernel exactly <(-a,n)>, giving a full extension equivalence. Replacing the lift changes a to a+nb, and the map E_(a+nb)->E_a fixing A and sending its distinguished lift to [(b,1)] respects the nth-power relation, so equivalence classes are exactly A/nA. The AC-qualified H^2 supplier is invoked under AC. Signs, quotient map, and product/quotient interfaces are consistent. No edit/stamp made by this reviewer.
